entry.evidence: This massif is thus key to understanding the tectonic affinity of this eastern part of the Protocarpathian basement.

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text) of Gawęda et al. 2022, checked against the published PDF

steps.action: The authors pose the aim: use new petrological, geochemical, U–Pb and P–T data to test correlations with the Romanian Carpathians and to place the protolith relative to the Baltica and Gondwana margins.
steps.quote: to interpret the paleotectonic setting of protolith rocks with respect to the evolution of the Baltica and Gondwana margins

steps.action: The authors sampled porphyroids and a phyllite (meta-tuff) from three outcrops of the Berlebash Suite, Dilove Nappe, plus one archive sample (UM-104a).
steps.quote: we sampled three rock types from Berlebash suite of the Dilove Nappe

steps.action: Petrography and microprobe mineral chemistry identify relict phenocrysts and two metamorphic assemblages, M1 and M2, in porphyroids and phyllite.
steps.quote: The metamorphic minerals can be grouped into two assemblages, representing two stages of development.

steps.action: Whole-rock XRF and ICP-MS analyses show rhyodacite-dacite, peraluminous, high-K calc-alkaline to shoshonitic compositions with VAG characteristics and negative Eu anomalies.
steps.quote: belong to the high-K calc-alkaline to shoshonitic series with VAG characteristics

steps.action: LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon dating gives concordia ages of 452.8 ± 1.5 Ma (UM-104a), 461.5 ± 1.6 Ma (SR10) and 584.7 ± 2.9 Ma (SR25C youngest rims), plus inherited Neoproterozoic to Archean cores.
steps.quote: 17 grains with oscillatory zonation yield a concordia age of 452.8 ± 1.5 Ma

steps.action: Secondary zircon standards Plešovice and WRS 1348 were run alongside the samples to check the U–Pb calibration; this check is reported only in the Methods.
steps.quote: Plešovice zircon (206Pb-238U age of 337.13 ± 0.37 Ma; Sláma et al. 61) which yielded a concordia age of 340.69 ± 0.99 Ma

steps.action: Peak M1 conditions were estimated with Ti-in-biotite thermometry and phengite barometry (560–600 °C, 600–900 MPa), and M2 conditions with phengite and ternary-feldspar thermometry (200–250 MPa, 222–384 °C).
steps.quote: Pressure estimates based on the muscovite (Ms1) chemistry are c. 600–900 MPa

steps.action: The M2 temperatures were cross-checked with a THERIAK DOMINO phase diagram and three independent chlorite geothermometers, which agree.
steps.quote: range from 280 to 360 °C (Table 3), which is in agreement with the phase diagram constraints

steps.action: M2 retrogression was correlated with the Romanian Alpine retrogression dated at c. 95 Ma (Culshaw et al.), and its timing was assumed without direct dating.
steps.quote: as there is a continuation in the nappe structure we assume a similar origin and timing for M2 retrogression

steps.action: From discrimination diagrams (Fig. 4) and trace-element anomalies (Fig. 5), the porphyroid protolith was inferred to be arc-related with a crustal component; zircon saturation temperatures were 823–892 °C.
steps.quote: is likely associated with an arc-related tectonic setting (Fig. 4c, d), which is supported by the negative Ta and Nb anomalies

steps.action: The new ages were compared with published ages of Ordovician meta-igneous bodies in Romania (Rodna) and the Gemericum, and they partly overlap.
steps.quote: partly overlap in age with similar meta-igneous bodies dated in the Romanian segment of the Eastern Carpathians

steps.action: The phyllite SR25C was interpreted as a Neoproterozoic arc-related meta-tuff, with 584.7 Ma as the maximum eruption age.
steps.quote: The U–Pb zircon concordia age of 584.7 ± 2.9 Ma is interpreted as the maximum estimate for the eruption age.

steps.action: Two rival scenarios taken from the literature are stated: a peri-Gondwanan arc with Cenerian docking (Balintoni and Balica), and an East Avalonian arc accreted to Baltica at the Tornquist closure.
steps.quote: allow us to speculate on possible tectonic scenarios (primarily a Baltican vs Gondwanan affinity)

steps.action: The Gondwana rival's Nd TDM evidence was compared with Sarmatian (Baltica) mantle-extraction ages and shown not to discriminate between the rivals.
steps.quote: However, the southern portions of Baltica (i.e. Sarmatia), also show similar c. 2.0 Ga mantle extraction ages

steps.action: The authors derived what the Avalonian/Baltica scenario expects: an active margin with inherited old crust, and c. 2.0 Ga Nd model ages inherited from a Sarmatian-type component.
steps.quote: can be interpreted as inherited from a Sarmatian-type crustal component, typical of many Avalonian terranes

steps.action: The Variscan and Alpine history of the massif was identified as the discriminating test between the two scenarios.
steps.quote: The key to resolving differences between these two scenarios is the Variscan and Alpine history of the Marmarosh Massif.

steps.action: The authors derived the Gondwana rival's prediction: docking with Baltica must then have happened in the magma-rich Variscan cycle, which should leave Variscan magmatism.
steps.quote: If it was not during the Caledonian orogenesis, the only other plausible timing for docking is during the Variscan cycle

steps.action: The prediction was compared with published work: no Variscan granitoids or volcanics are known in the massif, and late Variscan to Permian–Triassic metamorphic ages are attributed to distant events.
steps.quote: both in the Ukrainian and Romanian portions of the Marmarosh Massif no Variscan granitoids/volcanics have been found

steps.action: The authors keep the Avalonian provenance with Caledonian docking to Laurussia/Baltica as the scenario supported by the evidence.
steps.quote: All these facts thus support the second scenario, with an Avalonian provenance for the Marmarosh Massif (Fig. 9)

steps.action: The Cenerian / East Gondwana scenario is rejected in the conclusions.
steps.quote: rather than Cenerian orogenic events on the margin of East Gondwana

No review file supplied; acknowledgements mention editor and two reviewers

end.claim: The Dilove Nappe porphyroids record an early Caledonian (Ordovician, 453–461 Ma) volcanic arc accreted to Baltica during closure of the easternmost Tornquist Ocean, rather than Cenerian events on the East Gondwana margin.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the Gondwana scenario's required Variscan docking with the published absence of Variscan granitoids and volcanics in the massif is what tips the verdict toward the Baltica/Avalonia scenario.

gates.evidence: Sampling and analyses (§2 ¶5, §3–4) are described without a directing hypothesis; the two scenarios appear only in the Discussion (§5.3 ¶1). The Gondwana rival is rejected by an argument from the absence of Variscan magmatism in cited literature (§5.3 ¶4), not by a new test the claim could have failed. Nothing is reported as fixed before the data.

imports.item: LA-ICP-MS (laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry) with IOLITE data reduction
Scanning electron microscope BSE and cathodoluminescence imaging
Gibbs free-energy minimisation for equilibrium phase diagrams (THERIAK DOMINO)

limits: No review file or earlier version was supplied, so the review sequence is not coded, although the acknowledgements say the editor and two reviewers' comments led to a clearer presentation. The tectonic verdict rests on an argument from absence (no Variscan magmatism found), and the evidence for that absence is cited, not produced here. The new data constrain the age and setting of the arc but do not by themselves discriminate Baltica from Gondwana (inference). The Plešovice secondary standard came out at 340.69 ± 0.99 Ma against a reference of 337.13 ± 0.37 Ma, an offset of about 1% that is not discussed. Several internal inconsistencies appear in the document. §5.2 ¶2 cites Fig. 7d for the SR25C age, which is in Fig. 7f. The Table 3 footnote cites Jowett (1995), while the text cites Jowett (1991). The Table 5 caption refers to 'the exotic block from Pluskawka microgranite', apparently carried over from another paper (inference). In Table 4, SR11 and SR25C share identical ΣREE, Eu/Eu* and CeN/YbN values (possible copying error, inference). The stated SiO2 range (64.72–68.06 wt.%) excludes SR25C at 69.65. M2 timing is assumed from Romanian dating, not measured. Sub-claims and their statuses: the zircon ages (452.8, 461.5 and 584.7 Ma) are estimate_with_resolution; the M1 and M2 P–T conditions are estimate_with_resolution; the arc-related protolith is best_explanation; the correlation of the Dilove Nappe with the Romanian Bucovinian Nappe is best_explanation.

disagreements.target: Balintoni and Balica 2013; Balintoni et al. 2014 (peri-Gondwanan arc docked during Cenerian events)
disagreements.support: The Gondwana scenario would require Variscan docking, but no Variscan granitoids or volcanics are known in the massif (cited literature).
disagreements.quote: All these facts thus support the second scenario, with an Avalonian provenance for the Marmarosh Massif (Fig. 9)

disagreements.target: Balintoni and Balica (2013): c. 2.0 Ga Nd TDM model ages imply east (peri-) Gondwanan provenance
disagreements.support: Sarmatia (southern Baltica) shows similar c. 2.0 Ga mantle-extraction ages (Bogdanova et al. 2015), so the Nd ages do not single out Gondwana.
disagreements.quote: However, the southern portions of Baltica (i.e. Sarmatia), also show similar c. 2.0 Ga mantle extraction ages

disagreements.target: Cenerian back-arc closure interpretation applied to the Alps and Central Western Carpathians (Zurbriggen 2017; Putiš et al. 2008; Vozárová et al. 2010; Burda et al. 2021), as extended to the Bucovinian nappe
disagreements.support: The authors reject extending that framework to the Marmarosh Massif, on the same Variscan-absence argument.
disagreements.quote: rather than Cenerian orogenic events on the margin of East Gondwana
